text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Attorney-general says the file on Limassol killings will remain open in spite of decision not to prosecute police.
- Tape evidence is insufficient to charge policeman with Limassol mob shootings.
- A miracle is needed to stave off water cuts, say agriculture ministry officials.
- Right wing Disy seeks help from President Glafcos Clerides to quell the mutiny in the party over candidates in municipal elections.
- Mediators from Britain and the U.S. are disappointed at responses from the two sides to their initiatives, describing both as being over cautious to attempts to breach the deadlock.
- Greece's National Defence Minister Akis Tsohatzopoulos arrives in Cyprus today for talks.
